messages:
Maya: heads-up team — large customer asked for GA readiness commitments: SLA for inference, per-route token billing, and a 24/7 emergency support window. Need quick alignment on scope and tradeoffs.

Devin: what are their latency targets, region, models, and typical seq lengths?

Maya: EU primary, p95 < 150ms for 512 tokens, steady qps ~150-250, short bursts to ~900 for 2-6m. Models: M-v2 family; they want minimal quality loss on fallbacks.

Sam: rough feasibility: Dedicated pinned pools + multi-AZ routing can hit that tail. Shared hosted pools will need reserved burst pools and fallback variants; tail will be riskier.

Taylor: pricing implication — per-route token billing + 24/7 support means either a new premium SKU or an SLA surcharge. Need finops to model margins.

Kelly: legal needs exact SLA metric definition, credit formula, and exclusions (maintenance, customer misconfig). Keep wording simple for MSA.

Devin: ops asks: per-route dashboards (p50/p95/p99), SLO burn-rate alerts, and an auto-rollback trigger if p95 > target for >5m. Also sample request/response captures for quality regression checks.

Sam: to scope engineering work I need: confirmed model version + seq histogram, decision Dedicated vs Hosted, SLA number & penalty model, emergency support hours, billing model, and required telemetry.

Maya: docs: onboarding guide + SRE runbook (routing, escalation, fallback behavior, billing examples). Target a focused docs sprint after scope locked — ~1 week.

Taylor: prioritization tradeoff — this will bump Optimize backlog ~2 sprints. Sales says pilot is ~$300k ARR Y1; is that enough to re-prioritize?

Priya: commercial confirms pilot revenue and strategic value for EU expansion. Customer expects a pilot window with clear exit criteria.

Sam: rough estimates: infra + routing + autoscale + fallback mapping -> 3-4w (2 infra engs + 1 runtime). SLA testing + burn-in -> 1w. Docs/legal in parallel -> 1w. End-to-end ~5 weeks with parallel work.

Maya: propose two offers to present: A) Dedicated Pilot: committed SLA (e.g., 99.9% availability + latency objectives), per-route token billing, 24/7 emergency support, contractual SLA credits, faster launch (~5w). B) Hosted Pilot: conservative SLA (99.5%), burst addon, limited emergency support (business hours + on-call), longer runway (~8w).

Kelly: legal: include credit cap, force majeure, scheduled maintenance notice, and explicit customer misconfig exclusion.

Devin: operational guardrails: require traffic ramp (48h), approved test harness, and rollback rule: sustained p99 > target for 10m -> failover + page. Also require sample payloads before load tests.

Sam: testing plan: (1) lab latency profiling, (2) staging soak with prod-like traffic, (3) pilot shadowing, (4) guarded cutover ramp. Need sample traces and seq hist by EOD to start.

Maya: action owners: Maya (spec + docs), Sam (infra & tests), Devin (monitoring & rollback), Taylor (pricing scenarios), Priya (sales + contract), Kelly (legal). Can owners commit to a spec + action plan in 48h?

Taylor: I'll produce quick SKU vs addon pricing delta and COGS impact.

Priya: I'll draft a succinct SLA bullet list for the MSA and confirm customer acceptance of pilot constraints.

Kelly: legal will draft a short SLA clause and credit calc once numbers are stable. No unlimited credits.

Maya: if we pick Dedicated (A), call out limited pilot capacity and clear exit criteria. If Hosted (B), be explicit about tail risk and longer validation.

Devin: include fallback mapping doc: primary -> quantized variant -> smaller model and list expected quality deltas in runbook.

legal-bot: ticket created: PILOT-9999 "EU customer GA readiness & SLA scoping" assigned to @Sam @Devin @Taylor

Maya: thanks all — reconvene after spec draft. :thumbsup:
